intro:
A picture that moves inside its frame as you scroll past it.

The frame stays where the layout puts it and the image moves within it, which is what separates a parallax from a thing sliding around the page.

It is the counterpart to [ScrollText](/docs/components/scroll-text) — the same scrubbed reveal, applied to an image.

examples.title: The four effects
examples.description: They are four different jobs. `parallax` drifts the image against the scroll so the frame reads as a window onto something further away; `zoom` settles it from slightly oversized to its natural size; `reveal` wipes it in from the bottom edge; `sequence` picks a frame out of a series, so the reader scrubs an animation with their thumb.
examples.code:
<ScrollCanvas source={{ uri }} effect="parallax" />
<ScrollCanvas source={{ uri }} effect="zoom" />
<ScrollCanvas source={{ uri }} effect="reveal" />
<ScrollCanvas sources={frames} effect="sequence" />

examples.title: Scrubbing a sequence
examples.description: Every frame stays mounted and its opacity is switched, rather than one image whose source is swapped. A swap crosses back into JS at each step and then waits on a decode, so a fast scrub shows the previous frame or nothing at all. Keep it to a couple of dozen frames — each one is a decoded bitmap held for as long as the canvas is mounted.

examples.title: Shape and travel
examples.description: `aspectRatio` sets the frame; `distance` multiplies how far the effect moves. A parallaxing image is drawn taller than its frame so the drift never exposes an edge — pushing `distance` far past `1` spends more of that budget than there is.
examples.code:
<ScrollCanvas source={{ uri }} aspectRatio={1} distance={1.6} />

<ScrollCanvas
  source={{ uri }}
  aspectRatio={21 / 9}
  className="rounded-none"
/>

versions.title: Parallax
versions.description: The image drifts against the scroll inside a frame that stays put. It is drawn taller than the frame so the drift never exposes an edge.

versions.title: Zoom
versions.description: It settles from slightly oversized to its natural size as the frame crosses the viewport.

versions.title: Reveal
versions.description: A wipe uncovers it from the bottom edge up. A cover that retreats rather than a height that grows — animating a height relayouts the image inside it every frame.

versions.title: Sequence
versions.description: The scroll position picks the frame, so the thumb scrubs the animation. Every frame stays mounted and switches opacity; swapping one image's source would cross into JS and then wait on a decode.

notes:
The frame clips, so the image can be oversized and moved without disturbing anything around it. `reveal` is a cover that retreats rather than a height that grows, because animating a height relayouts the image inside it every frame — and it is a wipe rather than a fade so the frame keeps its shape while it fills.

“Canvas” here is the frame the pictures move behind, not a drawing surface: nothing is rasterised and there is no `<canvas>` involved.

Under `useReducedMotion`, or with `enabled={false}`, the image renders plainly at rest.
